introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2023. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators are allowed. Formulae booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

questions.enonce_markdown: (i) In how many ways can 3 boys and 2 girls be chosen from a class of 6 boys and 4 girls? *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The boys and the girls are chosen independently, and the order of choice does not matter, so we use combinations and multiply.

Boys: $\binom{6}{3}=\dfrac{6\times5\times4}{3\times2\times1}=20$.

Girls: $\binom{4}{2}=\dfrac{4\times3}{2\times1}=6$.

Total number of ways $=20\times6=120$.

**There are 120 ways.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii) Expand $(1-2x)^{-1}$ in ascending powers of $x$, up to and including the term in $x^3$. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use the binomial expansion for a negative index, $(1+u)^{n}=1+nu+\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2!}u^2+\dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{3!}u^3+\cdots$, with $n=-1$ and $u=-2x$ (valid for $|2x|<1$).

- Term in $x$: $n u=(-1)(-2x)=2x$.
- Term in $x^2$: $\dfrac{(-1)(-2)}{2}(-2x)^2=1\times4x^2=4x^2$.
- Term in $x^3$: $\dfrac{(-1)(-2)(-3)}{6}(-2x)^3=(-1)(-8x^3)=8x^3$.

$$(1-2x)^{-1}=1+2x+4x^2+8x^3+\cdots$$

Check: this is the geometric series $1+r+r^2+r^3+\cdots$ with $r=2x$.

**$(1-2x)^{-1}=1+2x+4x^2+8x^3+\cdots$**
